chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the woman who gives birth from adultery, and no one knows of that except her guardian: Is it permissible for him to marry her off and remain silent about it, provided he has seen repentance or a good deed from her? He (peace be upon him) said: If he does not mention that to her husband, and then the husband learns of it afterwards, and wishes to take her dower from her guardian for what he concealed from him, then he has that right against her guardian. And the dower which she took for herself, the husband has no claim upon her regarding it, due to what she permitted of her private part. And if her husband wishes to keep her, there is no problem.
ai.seo_question: What are the marital rights and financial compensations when a wife conceals adultery from her husband?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding a woman who conceals prior adultery resulting in childbirth, establishing that the husband may claim the dower from her guardian as compensation for the deception. Crucially, the Imam clarifies that while the husband has the right to annul the marriage or keep her, choosing to retain her means he forfeits the right to reclaim the dower, illustrating the Shia legal principle of 'ikhtiyar' (choice) in marital continuity. This highlights the distinction between the financial penalty for deception and the personal right to maintain the marital bond.
